thread_title: S. x areolata 'flop top' Washington Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. x areolata 'flop top' Washington Co, AL

posts.body_html:
Here's a really beautiful primary hybrid that originates from our very own Brooks Garcia. It's quite vigorous and produces 2 solid flushes of pitchers: spring/summer traps and fall traps. Much like its alata and leucophylla parents, the fall pitchers are larger and more vibrant than the spring/summer traps.

Notice how S. leucophylla is more dominant in this cross than S. alata. Perhaps the "floppy top" is due to the alata genetics. Interestingly, the traps are darker red when they first open, and they slowly turn whiter as they age. This particular clone is rather vigorous, and produces an abundance of medium height pitchers.

Photos taken 9/12/14:



Different light, these photos barely do this plant justice...it's a lot more amazing in person:


Isn't this a beauty?! I'm a sucker for neat primary hybrids! This trap is a bit older and the color is at its peak:



This pitcher just opened up, and notice how it's a lot redder than the previous photo. Usually, traps get redder as they age, so this clone strikes me as rather peculiar:

posts.body_html: It seems a lot of areolata have the "reverse color" habit. Mine opens with red flushed veins, then brightens to almost pure green and white, with very contrasting almost black pencil veins.
